versions.localizedDescription: ## MCX360 Edition 1.1 ### New - **On-screen touch controls**, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with `touch_controls`, `touch_controls_opacity` and `touch_haptics` in `mc360.toml`. - **Save thumbnails**: your worlds now show a picture in the world list. - **Exit Game** now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen. ### Performance - Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds. - Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (`framerate_limit`, default 60). - The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores. - Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame. ### Fixes - Fixed random crashes after playing for a while. - Fixed choppy audio. - Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed. - Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing. ### Known issues - Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps. - The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save. - Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement. Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.

## What's Changed in v1.3 > **Note**: AirCard-iOS currently supports **iOS 27.0 and newer (iOS 27+)**. ### PosterBoard Wallpapers (.tendies) • Added support for importing and unpacking `.tendies` wallpaper archives. • Automatic PosterBoard container detection and active descriptor UUID preservation. • Integrated instant WebKit NeoSpring respring right after flashing (no device reboot required). ### Apple Wallet & Passcode Theming • Added PDF artwork generation for transit passes (Suica, Pasmo, etc.). • Fixed keypad preview framing and TelephonyUI cache paths. • Cleaned up passcode number localization pickers. • Removed sluggish button glide animations when scanning cards and copying logs. ### UI & Quality of Life • Centered action buttons and removed misplaced list divider lines across all tabs. • Removed disruptive import and install alert popups in favor of clean inline status logs. • Cleaned up the VPN status bar and removed redundant text labels. • General repository cleanup and project modernization.
Various improvements added, jit fixed A15 iOS 17.0 TrollStore Go to settings, JIT mode detected, and leave it on automatic, and bugs fixed

# DukeX v1.0.2 - Expanding the Xbox Experience DukeX v1.0.2 is our biggest step yet toward preserving the full original Xbox experience, not just the games. This release introduces the first native macOS build, expands XB.Live integration, and brings richer community features to both iOS and macOS. ## What's New - Native macOS release: DukeX is now available as a Mac Catalyst desktop build packaged with a nested Xemu fork, pairing desktop Xemu compatibility with the DukeX interface. - XB.Live Rich Presence and playtime tracking: friends can see what you are playing while DukeX tracks supported playtime sessions. - XB.Live messaging: threaded conversations, friend messaging, unread indicators, supported game invites, and existing Xbox inbox support now live inside DukeX. - XB.Live social expansion: friend requests, friend management, online presence, and deeper community integration are available from the Profile experience. - Activity Feed: XB.Live news, friend online status, friend achievement unlocks, and community updates now appear in a continuously refreshed timeline. - Controller Landscape Mode: on iOS, compatible controllers can switch DukeX into a controller-first browsing and launch experience. - Expanded AirPlay and external display support: big-screen play is more reliable across supported display configurations. ## Improvements - Improved achievements with Games, Apps, and Cores grouping plus updated artwork handling for XB.Live Core, DukeX Core, and special test titles. - Improved game tile spacing and cover handling across iOS and macOS. - Improved XB.Live cloud-save sync metadata with console identity v2, content-hash dedupe, and server-assisted cross-console restore handling. - Fixed achievement progress rounding so time-based achievements do not show 100% before they are actually complete. ## Availability - iOS: install `DukeX.v1.0.2.ipa` through StikStore, SideStore, or another supported sideloading workflow. - macOS: install `DukeX.macOS.v1.0.2.dmg` by dragging DukeX to Applications. - Hardware requirements on iOS remain Apple A14 Bionic or Apple M1 hardware or newer. - iOS 16.0 or later is supported, with iOS 16 support remaining experimental. ## Important DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, copyrighted content, signing certificates, or user games. Users must provide their own legally obtained files. DukeX is intended for legitimate emulation, preservation, testing, and personal library use.

# Iridium 0.1.1 In standalone Iridium, you can now add games from its folder in Files without opening the file picker. This release also makes it easier to import a pairing file for built-in JIT. Game support remains experimental. ## Download **[Download Iridium (.ipa)](https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/releases/download/v0.1.1/Iridium-unsigned.ipa)** Requires **iOS or iPadOS 18+**, JIT, and your own game files. You only need the IPA to install. ## Install 1. Sign and install the IPA with a compatible sideloading tool, including its helper extension, or import it into LiveContainer. 2. Open Iridium and configure JIT in **Launch Support**. 3. Select **Add Game**, choose a game folder and executable, then press **Play**. Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. ## What's new - **Add games without the file picker.** In standalone Iridium, put each game in its own folder under **On My iPhone/iPad → Iridium → Games**. Choose **Add Game → Find Games in Iridium Folder**, select the game, and confirm its executable. Iridium uses the files in that folder without copying them. - **Import a JIT pairing file from Files.** Put `pairingFile.plist` under **On My iPhone/iPad → Iridium → StikJIT**. Choose **Settings → Launch Support → Import Pairing File → Use File in Iridium Folder**. You can still choose a file directly. ## Known issues - Some games may fail to launch or have graphics, video, audio, or input problems. - Skyrim speech and mouse attack issues remain unverified in this build. - JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. <details> <summary>Source code, licenses, and build details</summary> ## Source and licenses The other release files are for source access, rebuilding, and download verification: - Download both `Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01` and `.part02` for the complete matching source package. - `Iridium-source-guide.zip` contains license notices and build/relink instructions. - `SHA256SUMS` verifies all four files above, including the IPA. Download all five release files into one folder, then run: ```sh shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS cat Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01 Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part02 > Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz ``` The source guide includes the checksum for the assembled archive and rebuild instructions. GitHub's automatic repository ZIP does not contain all required dependency sources. Source commit: bc5c30fc442f429e8be9001549300160a0934372 Build run: https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/actions/runs/36504918645 App and helper version: **0.1.1 (98.2)**. Source checks, build, and unsigned-package checks passed. These checks do not establish compatibility with every game or device. Apple compiler-runtime notice uncertainty and unsigned-IPA contractual authorization remain documented risks. See the license guide in `Iridium-source-guide.zip`. </details>
